steps.title: Open ADD on the job
steps.body: From the job, click + ADD at the bottom of the screen. The totals on the right — tax and fees included — are what you're about to collect.

steps.title: Choose Payment
steps.body: Pick Payment from the menu. This one screen handles deposits, full payments, cards, cash — all of it.

steps.title: Review the basics
steps.body: The Comment your customer sees is prefilled from your defaults, and Due By is set automatically. Adjust either if this payment needs something specific.

steps.title: Set the amount
steps.body: Amount due is selected by default for a full payment. Taking a deposit instead? Click Custom and enter the amount.
steps.note: Below the amount you'll pick how they're paying: your card processor (UrPay here), or Check, Cash, and Other for payments you just need to record.

steps.title: Charge the card on file
steps.body: Inside UrPay you get every card option: the customer's card on file, Tap/Insert/Swipe for in-person, a Payment Form for cards over the phone, or a payable invoice. Click the card on file to charge it.

steps.title: Tip and sign
steps.body: The confirm screen offers tip presets your customer can tap, then they sign right on the screen and you hit PAY.

steps.title: Confirm the charge
steps.body: One last check — the exact card being charged. Click YES and Urable processes it on the spot.

steps.title: Cash, check and everything else
steps.body: Not a card? Cash, Check and Other record the payment without processing it. In Preferences > Payment, add custom methods — Venmo, PayPal, Cash App, Zelle — so 'Other' payments get tracked by name.
steps.note: This screen also holds the auto-receipt toggle, past-due timing, and automatic resend for pending payment requests.

steps.title: Paid, signed, receipted
steps.body: The payment record shows it all: $2,884.00 Paid, the card used, date and time, the signature — and with auto-receipts on, your customer already has their copy. Amount due on the job: zero.
